\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{صرف} (sirf)}{صرف (sirf)}]{\ur{صرف} (sirf) — only}

\label{lesson:UR-C366-sirf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a change, then the Urdu for to land in trouble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{صرف}}
\textbf{\ur{صرف}} — \emph{sirf} — \textquotedblleft{}only\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{صرف} \ur{ایک} \ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{آپ} \ur{جائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sirf ek ṭikaṭ hai to āp jāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is only one ticket, you go.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{صرف}} (\emph{sirf}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṣirf}, \textquotedblleft{}pure, unmixed\textquotedblright{}: that and nothing else.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sirf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sirf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar sirf ek ṭikaṭ hai to āp jāiye.} — If there is only one ticket, you go.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a change, then the Urdu for to land in trouble, then say \emph{sirf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{صرف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Only\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سوائے} (sivāe)}{سوائے (sivāe)}]{\ur{سوائے} (sivāe) — except (\ur{سوائے} … \ur{کے})}

\label{lesson:UR-C366-sivae}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to land in trouble, then the Urdu for only.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سوائے}}
\textbf{\ur{سوائے}} — \emph{sivāe} — \textquotedblleft{}except (\ur{سوائے} … \ur{کے})\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sivāe is ke koī rāstā nahīṅ to chaliye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سوائے}} (\emph{sivāe}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{siwā}, \textquotedblleft{}other than\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اجازت} (ijāzat)}{اجازت (ijāzat)}]{\ur{اجازت} (ijāzat) — permission}

\label{lesson:UR-C366-ijazat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for only, then the Urdu for except.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اجازت}}
\textbf{\ur{اجازت}} — \emph{ijāzat} — \textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ابو} \ur{نے} \ur{اجازت} \ur{دی} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{جاؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\emph{agar abbū ne ijāzat dī to maiṅ jāūṅ gā.}

Feminine.

\textbf{\ur{اجازت}} (\emph{ijāzat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ijāza}, \textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہرگز} (hargiz)}{ہرگز (hargiz)}]{\ur{ہرگز} (hargiz) — on no account (with \ur{نہیں})}

\label{lesson:UR-C366-hargiz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for except, then the Urdu for permission.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہرگز}}
\textbf{\ur{ہرگز}} — \emph{hargiz} — \textquotedblleft{}on no account (with \ur{نہیں})\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{ہرگز} \ur{نہیں} \ur{جاؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish huī to maiṅ hargiz nahīṅ jāūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, I will on no account go.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہرگز}} (\emph{hargiz}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{hargiz}, \textquotedblleft{}ever\textquotedblright{}; beside \textbf{\ur{نہیں}} it means \textquotedblleft{}never, on no account\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hargiz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hargiz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bārish huī to maiṅ hargiz nahīṅ jāūṅ gā.} — If it rains, I will on no account go.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for except, then the Urdu for permission, then say \emph{hargiz} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منع} \ur{کرنا} (manā karnā)}{منع کرنا (manā karnā)}]{\ur{منع} \ur{کرنا} (manā karnā) — to forbid; to tell (someone) not to}

\label{lesson:UR-C366-mana-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for permission, then the Urdu for on no account.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منع} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{منع} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{manā karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to forbid; to tell (someone) not to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{استاد} \ur{نے} \ur{منع} \ur{کیا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{نہیں} \ur{کھیلیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ustād ne manā kiyā to ham nahīṅ kheleṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the teacher says no, we will not play.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{منع} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne mujhe manā kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منع} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{manā karnā}) is built from \emph{manā}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{manʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}holding back, prevention\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manā karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manā karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar ustād ne manā kiyā to ham nahīṅ kheleṅ ge.} — If the teacher says no, we will not play.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for permission, then the Urdu for on no account, then say \emph{manā karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{منع} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To forbid; to tell (someone) not to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
